speaker: Doctor
text: I am disregarding the previous erroneous diagnosis and the injection to focus on your actual symptoms of progressive walking difficulty, urinary incontinence, and speech issues. To narrow down the cause, have you noticed any changes in your cognitive function or memory recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing a gradual difficulty in walking over the past 3 months, requiring wheelchair assistance for the last month. Additionally, there is a history of urinary incontinence for 1 year and recent onset of speech slurring making communication challenging.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the classic triad of gait disturbance, urinary incontinence, and cognitive/speech changes, I suspect Normal Pressure Hydrocephalus. REQUEST TEST: CT Head

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the CT head is normal, we need to rule out other structural or inflammatory causes for this triad of symptoms. Have you experienced any recent headaches, vision changes, or neck stiffness that might suggest increased intracranial pressure or meningitis?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive difficulty walking. I also have Urinary incontinence, Slurred speech, Rigidity in limbs, Mild hand tremor, Orthostatic hypotension.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of rigidity, tremor, and orthostatic hypotension alongside your other symptoms strongly points toward Multiple System Atrophy rather than Normal Pressure Hydrocephalus. I will proceed with the diagnosis based on this clinical picture. DIAGNOSIS READY: Multiple System Atrophy
